area: Assessments record view and shared assessment detail panel

heuristicIssues.issue: Irreversible workflow actions (Approve assessment, Finalize assessment, Request revision, Remove assignment) fire on a single click with no confirmation, no summary of the note that will be attached, and the same shared textarea feeds every one of them; an empty 'Request revision' silently sends the placeholder note 'Revision requested.' so the engineer receives no reason.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:294 (one textarea 'Optional workflow notes'), :323 (REQUEST_REVISION with notes.trim() || 'Revision requested.'), :324 (APPROVE), :328 (finalizeAssessment), :383 (removeAssignment) — all wrapped in run() at :208-220 which has no confirm step.
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Wrap Approve/Finalize/Request revision/Remove in a confirm dialog that shows the target assessment id, the resulting state, and the note text; make notes required for Request revision (disable the button until notes.trim() is non-empty); give each action its own note field or a labeled note in the dialog.

heuristicIssues.issue: When state is REVISION_REQUESTED the Next-step card tells the engineer to 'Address the reviewer's comments' but the comments live only in the History card's notes box at the very bottom of the panel, inside a 420px nested scroll region; the engineer must remember to scroll down and find the right event.
heuristicIssues.evidence: assessmentModel.ts:84 (instruction text); AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:265 (renders it), :390 (history card max-h-[420px] overflow-auto), :400 (notes only rendered here).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: In the Next-step card, when state is REVISION_REQUESTED (or SUBMITTED for reviewers), render the latest event whose to_state matches and has notes as a quoted 'Reviewer comment — {actor}, {date}' block directly under the instruction sentence.

heuristicIssues.issue: Selecting a different rail card keeps the previous assessment's full detail (title, badge, pipeline, submissions) on screen until the new GET resolves; there is no loading flag for the detail, so for a moment the page shows a stale record next to a newly highlighted card. 'Loading assessment…' only appears when detail is null.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:73-85 (setDetail only after await getAssessment; no detailLoading state), :139-142 (placeholder gated on detail being null), :41 (loading covers list only).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Add a detailLoading state set in loadDetail; while true, either dim the panel (opacity-60 pointer-events-none) with a 'Loading Assessment #id…' strip or clear detail before fetching; use aria-busy on the right section.

heuristicIssues.issue: Submission summaries come from a single /submissions/page?limit=200 index; any submission outside the first 200 renders as bare 'Submission #id' in the rail, and as '—' for Status/Reporter/Created/Submitted in the detail table, with 'Open' instead of 'Review'. Search also silently skips those submissions. Nothing tells the user data is missing rather than empty.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:19 (limit=200), :21-23 (index failure swallowed), :66-67 (search only over found submissions); AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:346-357 (dashes and Open fallback), :442 (rail descriptor only when found).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: For the selected assessment, fetch its submissions by id (GET /submissions/:id for each of submissionIdsOf) or have AssessmentDetail embed submission summaries; when a summary is unavailable show 'Details unavailable' rather than '—' and hide the Review/Open verb distinction.

heuristicIssues.issue: Form controls have no accessible names, the error banner is not announced, the pipeline's current step is conveyed only by color and font weight, and buttons have no focus-visible style (only the search input has focus:ring).
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:105 (state select, no label), :109 (search input, placeholder only; focus:ring present), :118 (error div without role=alert), :124/:142 (loading text without aria-live); AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:90-103 (no aria-current, dots aria-hidden, active = font-bold only), :126-128 (btn constants with hover: but no focus-visible:), :298-313 and :370 (unlabeled selects), :342-343 (table without caption/scope).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Add aria-label to the select/search/work-mode selects, role='alert' on the error banner, aria-live='polite' on loading/empty text, aria-current='step' plus a visually-hidden 'Current step' on the active pipeline li, and 'focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-[var(--brand)]' in the btn/btnPrimary/btnGood constants.

heuristicIssues.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
heuristicIssues.issue: The same record is described in different vocabularies within one screen: rail says 'Office NORTH · D03' while the header says 'North GeoTech Office · District 03'; submission statuses are raw codes ('SUBMITTED') while assessment states are humanized ('Submitted for review'); history event types are mechanically title-cased codes ('Delegate Branch'); the card hint introduces 'GISA form' as a synonym for 'technical submission'.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:434 vs :234 and :53-61; :353 (SubmissionStatusBadge raw status) vs assessmentModel.ts:51-63; :396 with assessmentModel.ts:65-68 (humanizeCode); :336 and :339 ('GISA form').
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Use officeLabel() and 'District {n}' in the rail card (or short codes in both places); map submission statuses through a label table like assessmentStateLabel; add an event-type label map ('Delegated to branch', 'Engineer assigned'); pick one term ('technical submission') and drop 'GISA form' or put it once in parentheses.

heuristicIssues.issue: A deep link to an assessment that is not in the current filtered list (deleted, not permitted, or filtered out) silently selects the first record with no message; and after Refresh, if the selected record's state no longer matches the active state filter, the selection silently jumps to another record. Filters and search are not in the URL, so a reload or shared link loses them.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:71 (selectedId falls back to filtered[0]), :38-39 (query/stateFilter in local state only), :96-99 (refreshAll keeps filters).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: When routeId is set but not in `items`, render a 'Assessment #id was not found or you do not have access' panel instead of falling back; when it is in items but filtered out, auto-clear the filter with a notice; persist stateFilter and q in useSearchParams.

heuristicIssues.issue: Up to 1000 assessments are loaded into one scrolling rail with no sort control, no pagination, and no 'waiting on me' shortcut; ordering is whatever the server returns, so finding the most recently updated or the oldest-stalled record requires scanning.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:49 (limit: 1000), :60-69 (client-side filter only), :123 (flat overflow-auto list); api/assessments.ts:103-116 supports state/office/queue params that the page does not use.
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Add a sort select (Updated desc default, District, State, Waiting on) applied in the filtered memo, group the rail by state or district, and use the API's queue/office_code params for a 'Mine' / office chip row.

heuristicIssues.issue: Repeated furniture: the 'N of M assessments' count appears twice 12px apart; the read-only banner is permanent and undismissable; every non-actionable record repeats 'Actions for this step are performed from My Work by the responsible role.'; the submissions table carries a raw 'User #id' Reporter column and an Action column that duplicates the descriptor link.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:110 and :122 (duplicate count), :114-116 (banner); AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:270 (repeated sentence), :354 (Reporter 'User #id'), :352 and :357 (two links to the same /submissions/:id).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Keep the count only in the rail header; collapse the banner to a one-line hint beside the title (or dismiss via localStorage); drop the per-record sentence in favour of a small 'Owner: {role}' tag; remove Reporter until the API returns a name; drop the Action column and make the descriptor link visibly a link.

heuristicIssues.heuristic: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
heuristicIssues.screen: Assessment detail panel (work mode via My Work) + record view
heuristicIssues.issue: All errors — list load, detail load, option fetch, and action failures — are funnelled into a single string at the top of the page above the rail, far from the control that failed, and the text is the raw server 'detail' message; a failed Approve in work mode shows nothing near the button.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:204 (option fetch → onError), :216 (action failure → onError); AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:118 (single banner), :140 (onError={setError}).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Keep a local actionError state inside AssessmentDetailPanel and render it inline under the action row with role='alert'; map common statuses (403 → 'You are not assigned as reviewer on this assessment', 409 → 'State changed — refresh').

heuristicIssues.issue: The pipeline shows six steps with dots but no dates or owners even though the API supplies per-step timestamps and ASSESSMENT_PIPELINE carries owner names; the only timing visible is 'Updated …' in the header and the History card at the bottom. Non-selected rail cards always say 'Waiting on Assigned Engineer' because assignments are only known for the loaded detail.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:84-105 (pipeline renders label only); api/assessments.ts:39-44 (office_delegated_at … approved_at unused); assessmentModel.ts:19-26 (owner field unused by Pipeline); AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:128 and assessmentModel.ts:74-75 (engineer name only for selected card).
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Under each done step render the matching timestamp (short date) and under the active step the owner; have the list endpoint include assigned engineer name (or map assigned_engineer_user_id through a small user cache) so rail cards can show the person.

heuristicIssues.issue: Two date formats sit in one card ('Sep 5, 2026, 3:04 PM' in Created/Submitted columns vs the 2-digit date embedded in the descriptor from buildSubmissionDisplayTitle), and three button sizes coexist in the area (toolbar py-2 text-sm, panel py-1.5 text-xs, reviewer select py-1 text-xs).
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:39-51 (formatTimestamp) vs :347 (descriptor with created_at), :126-129 vs :370; AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:111.
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Pass created_at into the descriptor only in the rail and omit it in the table (Created column already shows it), or format both through formatTimestamp; unify buttons on one size token (text-sm py-2 min-h-10).

heuristicIssues.issue: The 'Review' primary-styled button appears for every SUBMITTED submission regardless of the viewer's role or mode, inviting non-reviewers (and record-mode viewers) to click into a submission they cannot review.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:357 (status === 'SUBMITTED' ? btnPrimary 'Review' : btn 'Open'); permissions.review is computed at :155 but not consulted here.
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Show 'Review' with btnPrimary only when mode === 'work' && permissions.review; otherwise 'Open' (or remove the column and rely on the descriptor link).

heuristicIssues.issue: Page title, AppShell h1 and document.title stay 'Assessments' whether the user is on /assessments or /assessments/123 reached from an incident or event group; no breadcrumb indicates the selected record.
heuristicIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:102 (static title); no document.title assignment in either file.
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Set document.title to 'Assessment #id · Incident #n — ERIS' when detail loads and add a 'Assessments › #id' breadcrumb or update the AppShell title prop.

heuristicIssues.issue: Option labels '{full_name} · {email}' in the delegate/assign selects double the width of native option text and are hard to scan on phones; the reviewer select omits email, so the two selects disagree.
heuristicIssues.recommendation: Show full_name only, and disambiguate duplicates by appending the email only when two options share a name.

responsiveIssues.issue: Rail and detail stack vertically (split grid only at xl); the rail can be 860px tall, so after tapping a card the URL changes but the detail is off-screen below the rail — nothing scrolls it into view (scrollIntoView only targets the rail card). A first-day user taps and sees no visible change.
responsiveIssues.fix: Below xl, switch to a master/detail navigation: when routeId is set render only the detail with a sticky 'Back to list' bar; when not set render only the rail. Minimum patch: `max-h-[40vh] xl:max-h-[860px]` on the rail and a useEffect that scrolls the detail section into view (block:'start') on selectedId change when window.innerWidth < 1280.

responsiveIssues.issue: Toolbar wraps to 3-4 rows: select, then search (min-w-40 forces a wrap at 343px content width), then the count span and Refresh on separate lines; the read-only banner adds ~60px more before the rail.
responsiveIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:104-111 (flex flex-wrap, no ordering/width classes), :109 (min-w-40 flex-1), :114-116.
responsiveIssues.fix: Search: `order-first w-full sm:order-none sm:w-auto sm:flex-1`; select and Refresh: `flex-1 sm:flex-none`; move the count into the rail header only; collapse the banner to `hidden sm:block` with a short 'Read-only · act in My Work' pill next to the title on phones.

responsiveIssues.issue: Pipeline needs ~504px (6 × min-w-[74px] + 5 × min-w-3 connectors) inside ~311px of card width, so it scrolls horizontally with no scroll hint; 'Approval' and 'Finalized' are off-screen and the active step may be too.
responsiveIssues.fix: Render a vertical stepper below md (`flex-col md:flex-row`, connectors become a left border) or a compact 'Step {n} of 6 · {label}' progress bar on phones; if the horizontal version stays, add `snap-x` and scroll the active step into view on mount.

responsiveIssues.issue: The Technical submissions table has 7 columns (~800px natural width); on a 375px phone the Status badge and the right-aligned Review/Open action are off-screen behind an overflow-x-auto with no visual cue.
responsiveIssues.fix: Below md render each submission as a stacked row card (descriptor link, status badge, 'Created · Submitted' line); at md+ show the table with `hidden lg:table-cell` on Reporter/Created/Submitted; drop the Action column entirely.

responsiveIssues.issue: All action buttons are ~28px tall (px-3 py-1.5 text-xs) and the Add-reviewer select is ~24px (px-2 py-1 text-xs) — below the 44px touch guideline; the Delegate row puts two flex-1 selects and a button in one wrapping row so the button lands alone on a third line.
responsiveIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:126-129 (btn constants and select), :370 (reviewer select), :296-306 (delegate row).
responsiveIssues.fix: Add `min-h-10 md:min-h-0 md:py-1.5` (or simply py-2 text-sm) to btn/btnPrimary/btnGood and both selects; lay the delegate controls out with `grid gap-2 sm:grid-cols-[1fr_1fr_auto]` so the selects stack on phones and the button spans full width.

responsiveIssues.issue: Hover-only affordances: rail cards change border/background only on hover, the submission descriptor link is ink-colored and only turns brand on hover, and buttons rely on hover:bg — on touch there is no pressed or focus feedback and links are not recognisable as links.
responsiveIssues.evidence: AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:447 (hover:border/hover:bg on rail card), :352 (text-[var(--ink)] hover:text-[var(--brand)]), :126-128 (hover: only).
responsiveIssues.fix: Give the descriptor link `underline decoration-[var(--line)] underline-offset-2` and a trailing chevron; add `active:bg-[var(--panel-soft)]` and `focus-visible:ring-2` to cards and buttons; keep the active card's brand border as the selected cue.

responsiveIssues.issue: Three independent scroll regions on one page: the rail (overflow-auto inside max-h-[860px]), the History card (max-h-[420px] overflow-auto), and the document; on trackpads and touch the scroll target is ambiguous and users get 'stuck' inside the rail.
responsiveIssues.fix: Remove the History max-height (collapse the card by default with a 'Show N events' toggle instead); apply the rail max-height only at xl and make it viewport-relative: `xl:sticky xl:top-4 xl:max-h-[calc(100vh-7rem)]`.

responsiveIssues.issue: At 768×1024 (portrait) the AppShell renders the full nav card above the content and the rail/detail still stack, so the toolbar starts about one screen down and the detail sits below up to 860px of rail; at 1024×768 (landscape) the 256px sidebar appears (lg) but the split is gated at xl, leaving ~740px of content stacked vertically with the detail below the fold.
responsiveIssues.evidence: AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:120 (xl breakpoint for the split), :121 (860px rail); AppShell sidebar at lg per inventory (ui/AppShell.tsx:155-156).
responsiveIssues.fix: Move the split to lg with a narrower rail: `lg:grid-cols-[minmax(260px,0.8fr)_minmax(0,1.6fr)]`, and at lg cap the rail to `lg:max-h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] lg:sticky lg:top-4`; on portrait tablets (768-1023) use the phone master/detail behaviour.

responsiveIssues.issue: At 768px content width (~720px inside cards) the 7-column submissions table still overflows horizontally, hiding the Action column; at 1024px landscape with the lg split proposed above the detail column is ~440px wide and both the table and the 504px pipeline overflow.
responsiveIssues.fix: Use `hidden xl:table-cell` for Reporter and Created, `hidden lg:table-cell` for Submitted; make pipeline step min-width `min-w-[56px] lg:min-w-[74px]` and allow the label to wrap (`whitespace-normal`) below xl.

responsiveIssues.issue: At 1440×900 the fixed 860px rail exceeds the ~760px of viewport left under the sticky header, so the page and the rail both scroll and the rail's lower cards are only reachable after scrolling the page; the rail is not sticky, so when reading a long detail (history + table) the list scrolls away.
responsiveIssues.fix: Replace the fixed height with `xl:sticky xl:top-4 xl:max-h-[calc(100vh-6rem)]` so the rail always fits the viewport and stays visible while the detail scrolls.

responsiveIssues.issue: The header title flips from 'Incident #n technical assessment' to 'Incident #n · {title}' when the incident GET resolves after the assessment GET, causing a layout shift of the badge row and pipeline on every selection.
responsiveIssues.fix: Reserve the title line height (`min-h-[1.75rem]`) and render a subtle skeleton for the title until context resolves, or have the list/detail API include incident_title so no second request is needed.

dataDensity.reason: Primary narrowing control for up to 1000 records; directly serves 'find where an assessment is'.
Only free-text path to a specific record by id, incident, district or submission descriptor (assessmentModel.ts:142-166).
Exact duplicate of the rail header count 12px below (line 122); the rail header is the natural place for it.
Feedback that a filter is active, positioned where the list is.
Useful once for a first-day user, then permanent furniture; collapse to a one-line hint or a dismissible tip.
Only way to pick up state changes made by other roles; keep, but as a compact icon+label on phones.
Only failure feedback; needs role=alert and inline placement for action errors.
Record identity used in every cross-link.
Assessments are meaningless without the incident; ideally add the incident title when the list API can supply it.
Chiefs scan by office/district; align wording with the header (officeLabel / 'District').
Main scanning cue for pipeline position.
Answers 'who is blocking this' without opening the record — core to the second primary task.
Secondary context that adds a third line to every card; show only the count ('2 submissions') and leave descriptors to the detail.
Distinguishes empty from loading; extend to a per-selection loading state.
Record identity.
Only human-readable incident label in the area.

dataDensity.element: Meta line: office label · District · Updated
dataDensity.reason: Routing context and freshness; compact single line.
Fastest read of state; duplicates pipeline but is the anchor for the badge vocabulary used in the rail.

dataDensity.element: Header links: Open incident / View on map / Event Group #gid
dataDensity.reason: Third primary task (jump to incident, map, event group); three small pills is acceptable.
Visual progress; enrich with per-step dates from the API rather than adding another element.
Already progressive (only when set) and explains an unusual routing.
Terminal-state confirmation with timestamp.
Single most important coordination line; in record mode the sentence could be shortened since it describes someone else's task.

dataDensity.element: Record-mode sentence 'Actions for this step are performed from My Work by the responsible role.'
dataDensity.reason: Repeats the page-level banner on every non-actionable record; the 'Waiting on {role}' line already says who acts.

dataDensity.element: Record-mode CTA 'This step is yours — act on it in My Work'
dataDensity.reason: Only bridge from browsing to acting for the responsible user.

dataDensity.element: Work-mode 'No actions for your role on this step.'
dataDensity.reason: Explains an otherwise empty action area.
Explains why Submit is disabled — good error-prevention copy.
Should appear inside the confirm step of the specific action (or per action) rather than as one always-visible box shared by six actions.
Email only needed to disambiguate duplicate names; show name only by default.
Count of attached forms is the engineer's and reviewer's key number.

dataDensity.element: Card hint 'All GISA forms attached to this assessment's incident'
dataDensity.reason: Introduces a second term for the same object and adds a line to the card header.
Fold '#id' into the descriptor cell as a prefix; a separate column wastes width on tablets.
Human label and the primary way to open the form.
Reviewers need to see which form is SUBMITTED; humanize the code.
Raw user id has no meaning to a chief; reinstate only when the API supplies a name.
Already embedded in the descriptor date; show on lg+ only or in the row's expanded state.
Reviewers use it to judge queue age; hide below md only.
Same destination as the descriptor link in the same row; the 'Review' emphasis is wrong for non-reviewers anyway.
Who is accountable for each role — needed for the 'who is it waiting on' task.
Contact info is secondary; show as a mailto icon or on hover/expand to keep rows to one line on phones.

dataDensity.element: Assignments card: Add reviewer select + Add (work mode)
dataDensity.reason: Only place chiefs manage reviewers; keep but enlarge controls.
Necessary management action; add confirmation.

dataDensity.element: History card (events with actor, timestamp, from → to, notes)
dataDensity.reason: Audit trail rarely needed on first read; collapse by default with the count in the header, and surface the latest reviewer note in the Next-step card instead.
Mostly implied by the event type; keep only when from/to differ from the obvious transition (revision loops).

quickWins: Delete the toolbar count span (AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:110) and keep the rail header count (:122).

Add aria-label to the state select and search input (:105, :109), role='alert' to the error banner (:118), aria-live='polite' to the rail empty/loading text (:124) and detail placeholder (:142), aria-label to the work-mode selects (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:298, :302, :311, :370), and aria-current='step' on the active pipeline li (:90).
Append 'focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-[var(--brand)]' to the btn, btnPrimary and btnGood constants (:126-128) and to the rail card className (:447).

Gate Approve / Request revision / Finalize / Remove behind a confirm dialog (window.confirm at minimum) that repeats the assessment id and the note; disable Request revision until notes.trim() is non-empty (:323).
Add a detailLoading flag in loadDetail (AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:73-80) and dim the panel with aria-busy while a new record loads.
When routeId is set but not present in `items`, render a 'Assessment #id not found' card instead of falling back to filtered[0] (:71).
In the Next-step card, when state is REVISION_REQUESTED, render the notes of the latest event with to_state === 'REVISION_REQUESTED' as a quoted reviewer comment (:265, data from :393-400).
Use officeLabel() and 'District {n}' in the rail card (:434) so rail and header describe the office and district identically.
Remove the Reporter and Action columns from the submissions table and show 'Review' styling only when mode === 'work' && permissions.review (:354, :357).
Add 'hidden lg:table-cell' to the Created/Submitted th/td cells and drop the ID column into the descriptor cell (:343, :351).
Change the split breakpoint from xl to lg and replace the fixed rail height with 'lg:sticky lg:top-4 lg:max-h-[calc(100vh-7rem)]' (:120-121).
Below xl, scroll the detail section into view when selectedId changes (add a ref on the right section; :138).
Persist stateFilter and query in the URL via useSearchParams (:38-39) so shared links and reloads keep the filter.
Raise the submission index page size or fetch the selected assessment's missing submissions by id after loadDetail; replace '—' with 'Details unavailable' (:19; AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:353-356).
Make the read-only banner dismissible (localStorage flag) and hide it below sm (:114-116); drop the per-record 'Actions for this step…' sentence (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:270).
Render the pipeline as a vertical stepper below md ('flex-col md:flex-row') and show the matching *_at timestamp under each completed step (:84-105; api/assessments.ts:39-44).
Enlarge touch targets: base buttons on 'px-3 py-2 text-sm min-h-10 md:min-h-0 md:py-1.5 md:text-xs' and the reviewer select on the shared select class (:126-129, :370).
Set document.title to 'Assessment #id · Incident #n — ERIS' when detail loads (AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx after :75).
structuralChanges: Responsive master/detail navigation: below lg, /assessments shows only the rail (with filters) and /assessments/:id shows only the detail with a sticky 'Back to assessments' bar; at lg+ both render side by side with a sticky, viewport-bound rail. Share this scaffold with My Work instead of copy-pasting the grid (AssessmentWorkspacePage.tsx:120-136 vs MyWorkPage rail).

Rail as a real worklist: server-side state/office/queue filtering via the existing listAssessments params, a sort control (Updated desc default, Oldest waiting, District), grouping by state, and cursor pagination or virtualization instead of a 1000-item single fetch; list endpoint to return incident_title and assigned engineer name so cards can show 'Waiting on Engineer · Name' and the incident title without loading the detail.

Restructure the detail into a single Status card: pipeline with per-step timestamps and owners (from office_delegated_at, engineer_assigned_at, submitted_at, review_requested_at, approved_at, finalized_at), the Next-step line, the latest reviewer/workflow note, and the record-mode CTA; History becomes a collapsed 'Activity' section at the bottom.

Work-mode action model: replace the one shared 'Optional workflow notes' textarea and immediate-fire buttons with per-action confirm sheets (Approve, Request revision with required comment, Finalize, Delegate/Assign with selected person summary, Remove reviewer) rendered inline with their own error state; notes and outcome are shown in the sheet before submission.

Submissions as responsive rows rather than a 7-column table: each row shows '#id · descriptor' link, humanized status badge, submitted date, and a role-aware primary action; below md rows stack as cards. Back it with AssessmentDetail embedding submission summaries (or /submissions?ids=) so the 200-item global index and its silent gaps are no longer needed.

Unify labels and formats through shared utilities: one formatTimestamp in utils, a submission status label map alongside assessmentStateLabel, an event-type label map, office names from the API (RoutingPreview.office_name) instead of the hardcoded OFFICE_NAMES table (AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:53-57), and a single button/size token set used by the toolbar, panel pills and table.

Navigation context: breadcrumb 'Assessments › Assessment #id' with document.title, and a return-path parameter so Submission detail's back link returns to /my-work when the user arrived from the work queue rather than always to /assessments/:id.
